sections.overview: Falcipennis canadensis, the Spruce Grouse or Tétras du Canada, is a boreal forest grouse. AOS and IOC lists now use Canachites canadensis.
sections.identification: Males are dark with white-spotted flanks and a bright red eyebrow comb in spring; females are brown and mottled.
sections.habitat: It depends on conifer forests, including spruce, fir, jack pine and larch; denser cover is used in winter and more open habitat to raise chicks.
sections.diet: Adults eat conifer needles, especially spruce and pine; summer diet also includes berries, plants, fungi and insects.
sections.behavior: It is a resident bird, often tame, and males advertise territories with spring flutter flights and wing sounds.
sections.reproduction: Females nest on the ground and usually lay 5–7 eggs; incubation lasts about 20–24 days.
sections.ecology: The grouse depends on conifer forest mosaics and regenerating stands. AOS moved the species from Falcipennis to Canachites. IOC lists the same genus change.
sections.conservation: Quebec reports provincial rank S5 and slight Canadian increase since 1970, while warning that southern populations face forest loss.
